title: Skylight speed-range and machine-learning fishing alerts may have led Argentina's Prefectura Naval to intercept the Vanuatu-flagged XINRUN 579 on 5 January 2025, and a fine may have been paid
summary: Skylight reports that its speed alert and its machine-learning fishing alert led Argentina's coast guard to intercept a trawler on 5 January 2025, and that the vessel paid a fine.
account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA), Argentina's coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that speed as a sign of trawling. The coast guard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, which opened administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). This independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. On 3 March 2025 an NVIDIA Developer blog post reported that the coast guard interdicted the vessel and later fined it after Skylight alerted it. Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coast guard vessel. Skylight says that the case led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence. It says that the vessel paid the fine and the operational costs. The account quotes a retired PNA captain who coordinates EICEMAR, an interdisciplinary team for the control of maritime spaces and their resources. It also quotes the lead of the PNA's geographic information systems division. Both credit Skylight. The PNA release that Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive.
purpose: Real-time detection of suspicious vessel behavior and fishing activity to support maritime enforcement against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. The interception was the intended use.

ratings.reason: The PNA intercepted the vessel within hours and, per Skylight, issued its first international electronic fine with the fine and costs paid. The independent report confirms the interception and administrative proceedings.

The interception concerns one vessel among hundreds that operate at the edge of Argentina's exclusive economic zone each season, and no effect on fish stocks or on illegal fishing at large is reported.

ai_role.statement: Skylight's own account describes a two-stage AI contribution. A rule-based Speed Range Event flagged the vessel at under 6 knots inside an area of interest. 40 minutes later a Fishing Event from its machine-learning model, which detects longlining, trawling and squid jigging, reinforced the suspicion. PNA analysts then redirected a coastguard vessel. A retired PNA captain is quoted saying Skylight contributed directly to the decision. This is the maker's account, with the deployer's officers quoted inside it. The independent report (Agenda Malvinas, citing Pescare and official information) attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not name Skylight or AI. So the attribution to the AI output is not independently confirmed. The PNA release Skylight links to is not among the sources.

fields.summary: Skylight reports that its speed alert and its machine-learning fishing alert led Argentina's coast guard to intercept a trawler on 5 January 2025, and that the vessel paid a fine.
fields.account: On Sunday 5 January 2025 the Prefectura Naval Argentina (PNA), Argentina's coast guard, detected the Vanuatu-flagged trawler XinRun 579. It was in Argentina's exclusive economic zone off Caleta Olivia, Santa Cruz, sailing at under 6 knots. Local rules treat that speed as a sign of trawling. The coast guard vessel GC-25 Azopardo intercepted it. The captain was formally notified of an infraction under Law 24.922, which opened administrative proceedings (Agenda Malvinas, 8 January 2025, citing official information). This independent news report attributes the detection to the PNA's Sistema Guardacostas and does not mention Skylight or AI. On 3 March 2025 an NVIDIA Developer blog post reported that the coast guard interdicted the vessel and later fined it after Skylight alerted it. Skylight, the free AI maritime-monitoring platform of the Allen Institute for AI, published its own account on 31 March 2025. A rule-based Speed Range Event first alerted the authorities. A Fishing Event alert from its machine-learning model came 40 minutes later. PNA analysts redirected a nearby coast guard vessel. Skylight says that the case led to Argentina's first international electronic fine using AI-powered evidence. It says that the vessel paid the fine and the operational costs. The account quotes a retired PNA captain who coordinates EICEMAR, an interdisciplinary team for the control of maritime spaces and their resources. It also quotes the lead of the PNA's geographic information systems division. Both credit Skylight. The PNA release that Skylight links to is not found live or in the Internet Archive.
